key_insight: The temperature-induced band-gap bowing in FAxMA1−xPbI3 is mainly caused by anomalous electron-phonon coupling from mixed cage-tilt and FA cation rattler modes, with thermal expansion playing a secondary role.
engineering_relevance: Understanding and controlling this coupling helps predict and tune perovskite band gaps for more stable, temperature-robust solar cells and optoelectronic devices.
method: Temperature-dependent photoluminescence on FAxMA1−xPbI3 single crystals (x = 0 to 1)
Pressure-dependent photoluminescence to separate thermal expansion effects from electron-phonon effects
Interpretation of low-temperature phase behavior across orthorhombic and pseudotetragonal regimes
evidence_signal: The study combines temperature and pressure measurements across a compositional series of single crystals and finds that the electron-phonon term dominates the observed gap bowing.
watch_item: The proposed mechanism is inferred for low-temperature phases and may depend on stripe-domain formation and composition range, so device behavior may differ in real thin films or under operating conditions.
paper_title: Origin of the Temperature-Induced Gap Bowing of Formamidinium-Methylammonium Lead Iodide Perovskites: Role of Cationic Rattlers
